data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Manual (DM) provides guidance for cybersecurity incident management and reporting and describes essential preparations for effective incident management.
policy_statements.target: guidance for cybersecurity incident management and reporting

policy_statements.source_text: This DM supports compliance by the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA) with Federal laws, regulations, and guidance on cybersecurity incident management.

This DM serves as the foundation for Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices to develop and implement cybersecurity incident management procedures and plans that comply with Federal and Departmental requirements.
Major objectives of the cybersecurity incident management procedures in this manual are to:
Mitigate risks from incidents before substantial harm occurs;
Ensure coordination of and good communication about incident management activities within USDA and with external stakeholders; and
Provide timely notification and reporting to appropriate entities.
This manual is effective immediately and remains in effect until it is superseded or expired.
All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will align their procedures with this manual within 6 months of the publication date.
policy_statements.actor_name: All Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices
conditions: within 6 months of the publication date

policy_statements.source_text: The DM aligns with the Department’s cybersecurity incident management policy, Departmental Regulation (DR) 3505-005, Cybersecurity Incident Management.
Terminology in this DM will be used and interpreted as follows:
The term “misuse” broadly refers to improper usage of information or information resources in violation of rules, regulations, or policies;
The term “operational security” encompasses techniques and processes that protect less valuable information from disclosure to an adversary to protect more valuable information.

For example, disclosing only to those with a need to know that an incident has occurred so that an investigation to identify the intruder, and the information sought by the intruder can be investigated.
Operational security techniques focus on preventing information from being inadvertently disclosed to an adversary.
The objective of operational security techniques and processes prevent an adversary, for example, of knowing where information is located, how it is protected, or learning about mitigation plans;
The terms “potential,” “suspected,” and “imminent” with respect to threats and incidents are distinct.
“Potential” refers to a currently unrealized ability and is nearly synonymous with “possible” (e.g., a potential threat).

“Suspected” implies a slight indication that something might be true or there is a reasonable basis for believing so; in other words, incidents may be suspected, as opposed to being confirmed (positively identified) or actual.

“Imminent,” as explained by National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-61 Revision 2, Computer Security Incident Handling Guide, refers to a situation in which there is a factual basis for believing that a specific event is about to occur; attacks from a zero-day exploit of a vulnerability can be imminent;
cross_references: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Special Publication (SP) 800-61 Revision 2, Computer Security Incident Handling Guide

policy_statements.source_text: The terms “response” and “incident response” may be broad or narrow in meaning.
The broad meaning encompasses multiple incident management activities, including analysis, notification, mitigation or application of countermeasures, containment, eradication, and recovery.
The narrow meaning is any one of these activities.
NIST uses the terms “incident response” and “incident handling” as synonyms; and
The term “US-CERT” is used in this manual as a replacement for “the Federal information security incident center” identified in FISMA.

USDA experiences suspected and actual cybersecurity incidents daily, necessitating a framework for managing incidents supported by incident management plans, procedures, resources, testing, and training.

This DM draws on Federal requirements for incident management found in Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-130, Responsibilities for Protecting Federal Information Resources, July 28, 2016; FISMA; NIST SP 800-53 Revision 4, Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations; NIST SP 800-61 Revision 2; and other Federal regulations.
cross_references: Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Circular A-130, Responsibilities for Protecting Federal Information Resources, July 28, 2016
NIST SP 800-53 Revision 4, Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations

policy_statements.source_text: This manual encompasses reporting both cyber-related and non-cyber breaches.
All breaches that must be reported within USDA to the Agriculture Security Operations Division (ASOD) cybersecurity incident response team (CSIRT) and the USDA Privacy Office;
All cyber-related breaches that are reportable to the United States Computer Emergency Readiness Team (US-CERT); and
All major breaches that are reportable to Congress.

Nothing in this DM will alter the requirements for the protection of information associated with national security systems (NSS) such as those in the Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA), policies, directives, instructions, and standards issued by the Committee on National Security Systems (CNSS), or the intelligence community.
cross_references: Federal Information Security Modernization Act of 2014 (FISMA)

policy_statements.source_text: The procedures in this DM expand upon DR 3505-005, which addresses:

Appropriately managing suspected and actual incidents affecting USDA information resources, including specialized incident types such as breaches, criminal activity, or misuse, and classified national security information (CNSI) spillage;
Safeguarding sensitive incident information;
Detecting potential compromises and exploits;
Timely reporting of incidents internally to the ASOD CSIRT, externally to US-CERT, and notifying Congress of major incidents;
Maintaining well-tested incident management plans and procedures and providing appropriate resources for incident management; and
Providing awareness and training for incident management personnel and general users.
This Section describes Department-level incident management activities that should be leveraged to produce organization-specific incident management procedures.

The ASOD CSIRT operates as USDA’s central cybersecurity incident management group, coordinating incident management activities, sharing information with both internal USDA offices and external entities, and providing assistance to agencies and staff offices when requested.
policy_statements.resulting_status: USDA’s central cybersecurity incident management group

policy_statements.source_text: For certain types of incidents, the USDA Privacy Office, Core Incident Response Group (CIRG), OIG, Office of Homeland Security (OHS) Personnel and Document Security Division (PDSD), OHS Insider Threat Program, and other offices have incident management responsibilities.

policy_statements.source_text: Notification and reporting to Congress and OMB are covered in Sections 8 and 9.
The ASOD CSIRT coordinates incident management activities with other USDA offices.
It is staffed 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.
The ASOD CSIRT is USDA’s designated operational liaison with US-CERT.
The ASOD Director designates a primary and secondary point of contact in the ASOD CSIRT for all interactions with US-CERT.

The ASOD Director has the authority to appoint an incident commander for a major incident (which may be declared by USDA, Department of Homeland Security (DHS), or OMB) or when warranted by other circumstances.

policy_statements.source_text: The incident commander is then responsible for directing and managing the incident.

The ASOD Director or the designated incident commander, during complex or crisis-level incidents (that is, those that require non-routine response operations), sets priorities based on factors such as functional impact, information impact, recoverability, and resource availability and communicates those priorities and requirements for additional assistance or resources to the USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) or US-CERT.

conditions: during complex or crisis-level incidents (that is, those that require non-routine response operations)

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT must produce metrics about incidents for reporting to the President’s Management Council, OMB, or other Federal organizations such as:

Whether an incident or an attack successfully resulted in unauthorized access to, exfiltration of, manipulation of, harm to, or impaired the integrity, confidentiality, or availability of an information system or information that is stored on, processed by, or transiting an information system; and
Any public and internal notifications about an incident and the dates of those notifications.
The ASOD CSIRT deploys automated tools such as intrusion detection systems and network analysis software to support detection and analysis and runs them on a regular schedule.
The tools are configured to receive updates to indicators from their vendors.

When US-CERT issues an alert about a suspected or actual compromise with the potential to affect U.S. Government systems and provides indicators of compromise (IOC), the ASOD CSIRT must start IOC scans using the provided indicators within 24 hours.
conditions: When US-CERT issues an alert about a suspected or actual compromise with the potential to affect U.S. Government systems and provides indicators of compromise (IOC)
within 24 hours

policy_statements.source_text: If the ASOD CSIRT confirms a compromise has occurred, this information must be reported back to US-CERT.

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT also participates in DHS’s EINSTEIN program to detect security incidents and collect incident information for analysis.
The ASOD CSIRT reports only cyber-related incidents to US-CERT.
Non-cyber incidents (such as exposure of printed documents containing PII) are not reported to US-CERT.
The ASOD CSIRT must report the following to US-CERT within 1 hour:
conditions: within 1 hour:

policy_statements.source_text: Suspected or actual exposure or compromise of cyber-based PII;
Suspected or actual cyber incidents related to criminal activity or misuse;
Suspected or actual incidents of CNSI spillage and compromise of classified systems; and
All confirmed incidents of compromise to the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of USDA information, information systems, or information services.
Reporting to US-CERT within 1 hour is mandatory and must not be delayed to provide or gather other details about the incident such as root cause, threat vector, or mitigation actions taken.

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT must report each incident separately because US-CERT does not accept reports of multiple incidents in a single submission.
The ASOD CSIRT emails the reports to US-CERT from its incident ticketing system.

policy_statements.source_text: Required information for reporting to US-CERT can be found in the DHS, US-CERT Federal Incident Notification Guidelines.

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT ensures that each reported incident is categorized, prioritized, and contains all other required information prior to sending it to US-CERT.

policy_statements.source_text: As additional information is discovered and gathered about an incident, the ASOD CSIRT provides updates to US-CERT.

The ASOD Director or the incident commander may, based on the severity of an incident, activate the standing Federal Network Authorization, authorizing US-CERT to access relevant USDA networks and, if necessary, to provide on-site technical assistance.

policy_statements.source_text: See the following Sections for specific incident handling guidance:
Section 6g for specific guidance about breaches;
Section 6h for OIG related incidents; and
Section 6i for CNSI spillage.
For incidents involving spillage of CNSI, PII, or controlled unclassified information (CUI), all personnel must minimize damage to or further exposure of the information.

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT reminds personnel of the following protective actions when suspected or actual incidents involving these types of sensitive information are reported to them.
Specifically, personnel reporting spillage of CNSI, PII, or CUI must:
Not delete or forward any spilled information in any format, whether it is an email, attachment, hyperlink attachment, or hardcopy document; and
policy_statements.actor_name: personnel reporting spillage of CNSI, PII, or CUI

policy_statements.source_text: Take custody of the information to safeguard it from further unauthorized access until it can be secured by the proper authority.

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT ensures that the correct forms are used and properly completed for reporting incident details: Agriculture Department (AD)-3043, ASOC Incident Report, or AD-3038, Cyber Security Incident Report Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Incident.

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT ensures that actions are immediately performed to mitigate incidents or threats that have or potentially will have:
High functional impacts to all critical services and system users; or
Severe impacts to the integrity of USDA information or to information deemed to be classified, privacy-related, or proprietary.

The ASOD CSIRT ensures that compromised devices are disconnected from the USDA network, appropriately analyzed, and, if appropriate, restored to service in a secure configuration only after malware or other types of compromise are eradicated.
conditions: only after malware or other types of compromise are eradicated

policy_statements.source_text: ASOD CSIRT personnel, at the direction of the ASOD Director or the designated incident commander, collaborate and coordinate on a need-to-know basis with external entities such as Internet Service Providers (ISP), other incident response groups, affected external parties, or vendors of information technology (IT) products and services, about investigation and mitigation of incidents.

ASOD CSIRT personnel, with the concurrence of the USDA CISO, the ASOD Director, or the designated incident commander, notify external organizations affected by an actual or suspected incident (exploit or threat) originating from USDA.
policy_statements.target: external organizations affected by an actual or suspected incident (exploit or threat) originating from USDA

policy_statements.source_text: Different agencies, offices, and the CIRG have different responsibilities for issuing external notifications about incidents.
policy_statements.actor_name: Different agencies, offices, and the CIRG

policy_statements.source_text: The responsibility varies depending on the type of incident and the audience for the notification.

Examples of external communications include informing the public in general; notifying individuals affected by a breach; or alerting external parties affected by an actual or suspected incident originating from USDA.
This Section covers general information about external notifications; subsequent Sections describe the responsibilities for special types of incidents.
When external notifications are to be issued, the responsible agency or office must inform or consult with the Director of the Office of Communications (OC).
conditions: When external notifications are to be issued

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) and the Director of OC are jointly responsible for notification about major incidents at USDA that are issued to general public, the media, and external entities not directly affected by the incident.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Chief Information Officer (CIO) and the Director of OC
conditions: about major incidents at USDA that are issued to general public, the media, and external entities not directly affected by the incident

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT:
Monitors and tracks agency and staff office mitigation efforts;
Validates completion of the mitigation efforts;
Verifies that affected systems and devices are no longer a threat to the USDA network; and
Validates that all required reporting information has been provided.

The ASOD Director or the designated incident commander provides another level of oversight, ensuring that all incident handling activities are validated as complete, including additional reporting to US-CERT.
policy_statements.actor_name: ASOD Director or the designated incident commander
policy_statements.target: another level of oversight, ensuring that all incident handling activities are validated

policy_statements.source_text: Incidents may be reopened at the request of ASOD CSIRT personnel, the ASOD Director, the Senior Agency Official for Privacy (SAOP), the USDA Chief Privacy Officer (CPO), the Inspector General, or the Chief of OHS PDSD.
The ASOD CSIRT must provide notifications of suspected or actual exposure or compromise of PII to the following within 1 hour:
conditions: within 1 hour:

policy_statements.source_text: For cyber-related breaches, notify the US-CERT, the USDA Privacy Office, the agency or staff office CSIRT, and the OIG; and
policy_statements.target: US-CERT, the USDA Privacy Office, the agency or staff office CSIRT, and the OIG

policy_statements.source_text: For non-cyber breaches (e.g., hardcopy only), notify the USDA Privacy Office, the agency or staff office CSIRT, and the OIG.
policy_statements.target: USDA Privacy Office, the agency or staff office CSIRT, and the OIG

policy_statements.source_text: All incident management personnel receive direction and guidance regarding breaches, whether or not they are cyber-related, from:
The USDA CPO when the incidents are low impact;
conditions: when the incidents are low impact

policy_statements.source_text: The SAOP when the breaches are moderate and high impact; or
conditions: when the breaches are moderate and high impact

policy_statements.source_text: The CIRG when convened.
conditions: when convened

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT provides email notification of breaches to the USDA CPO and others, as directed by the CPO.
Files or emails containing PII should not be emailed or forwarded.

Details about breaches are documented on form AD-3038; the form has Sections to report unauthorized access and equipment containing PII that is lost or stolen (including seizure by a foreign government).
Care must be taken to ensure that PII related to actual or suspected incidents is handled properly and its use and disclosure is minimized to the greatest extent possible.
Procedures in the USDA Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Core Incident Response Group (CIRG) PII Breach Notification & Incident Response Plan (IRP) must be followed.
cross_references: USDA Personally Identifiable Information (PII) Core Incident Response Group (CIRG) PII Breach Notification & Incident Response Plan (IRP)

policy_statements.source_text: Actions directed by the CIRG or the USDA Privacy Office must be completed in the prescribed timeframe to meet notification guidance prescribed in OMB M-17-12, Preparing for and Responding to a Breach of Personally Identifiable Information.
cross_references: OMB M-17-12, Preparing for and Responding to a Breach of Personally Identifiable Information

policy_statements.source_text: The SAOP will be responsible for advising the Secretary of Agriculture whether and when to notify individuals potentially affected by a breach, in coordination with the:
CIRG when convened; or
CPO, when the CIRG is not convened.
The Secretary of Agriculture will make a final decision regarding whether to provide notification to individuals affected by a breach.

The CIRG, when convened, is responsible for requiring notifications to be developed, and reviewing and approving the content of notifications to all individuals impacted by exposure of their PII by USDA employees or contractors.
conditions: when convened

policy_statements.source_text: When the CIRG has not been convened, OC is responsible for breach notifications.
conditions: When the CIRG has not been convened

policy_statements.source_text: OC may delegate this responsibility to agency and staff office communication or public affairs offices.
Office of the General Counsel (OGC) must review and approve any notifications to individuals impacted by a breach in which the individuals are or were litigants.
policy_statements.target: and approve any notifications to individuals impacted by a breach in which the individuals are or were litigants
conditions: in which the individuals are or were litigants

policy_statements.source_text: Office of Human Resources Management (OHRM), in coordination with OC, is responsible for breach notifications to current and former USDA employees, retirees, and retirees’ survivors or designated dependents (e.g., spouses and minor or adult children).
Other types of breach notifications for which OC is responsible include:
Notifications to other impacted individuals, such as customers, grant recipients, or contractors; and
Notifications to the general public, the media, and external entities not directly affected by the incident.
The SAOP must certify by email that a moderate or high impact breach is closed.
The USDA CPO must approve closure of all other breaches.
ASOD CSIRT coordinates with OHS PDSD regarding all incidents involving foreign actors;
The ASOD CSIRT must immediately escalate to the OIG Technical Crimes Division (TCD), Special Agent in Charge via email or the OIG Hotline (202-690-1622):
All cyber investigations and incidents related to or potentially related to criminal activity;
Incidents related to fraud, waste, and abuse of information resources; and
Any incidents that involve law enforcement from any level of government (Federal, State, local, tribal, or territorial).
The ASOD CSIRT must report suspected or actual cyber incidents of criminal activity or misuse to US-CERT within 1 hour of notification or detection.
conditions: within 1 hour of notification or detection
policy_statements.target: suspected or actual cyber incidents of criminal activity or misuse

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT must report to OIG every incident that is reported to US-CERT.
policy_statements.target: to OIG every incident that is reported

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT and other incident management personnel must cooperate with OIG and law enforcement personnel to provide any support needed for criminal investigations and prosecutions.
policy_statements.actor_name: ASOD CSIRT and other incident management personnel

policy_statements.source_text: OIG and the ASOD CSIRT collaborate prior to taking possession of government furnished equipment (GFE) for investigations involving actual or suspected criminal activity or misuse.
conditions: prior to taking possession of government furnished equipment (GFE) for investigations involving actual or suspected criminal activity or misuse

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area Assistant CISOs and Information Systems Security Program Managers (ISSPM) must inform the ASOD CSIRT and provide specific guidance for handling GFE and information on that GFE when the agency or staff office is operating under a law specific to its mission, such as the Confidential Information Protection and Statistical Efficiency Act of 2002 (CIPSEA).
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area Assistant CISOs and Information Systems Security Program Managers (ISSPM)
cross_references: Confidential Information Protection and Statistical Efficiency Act of 2002 (CIPSEA)

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT must coordinate with agency and staff office personnel responsible for incident management, and employee relations or adverse personnel actions prior to taking possession of GFE for investigations or confirmed incidents.
conditions: prior to taking possession of GFE for investigations or confirmed incidents

policy_statements.source_text: OIG and the ASOD CSIRT will coordinate with other entities as applicable when taking possession of GFE.
Examples of applicable entities include:
Federal, State, local, tribal, or territorial levels of law enforcement agencies;
Other USDA agencies and staff offices affected or potentially affected by the incident; or
In cases that may lead to adverse personnel action, OHRM or agency or staff office personnel responsible for employee relations or adverse actions.
OIG is responsible for notifications about suspected and actual incidents with a connection or link to criminal or foreign actors.
The OIG or the ASOD CSIRT, after conferring and when appropriate, will notify law enforcement agencies;
The Inspector General (IG) is responsible for providing notifications, as appropriate:
To external parties affected by the incident; and
In coordination with OC and only when notification will not impact open criminal investigations, the general public, the media, and external entities not directly affected by the incident.
OHS PDSD:
Coordinates incident management with the ASOD CSIRT; and
Conducts official investigations of suspected or actual CNSI spillage incidents and incidents affecting classified systems.
Contact information is:
OHS PDSD: Call 202-720-7373 or email <pdsd@dm.usda.gov>; the phone is staffed Monday through Friday, 7 a.m. until 5 p.m. (Eastern Time); and
ASOD CSIRT: Call 866-905-6890 or email <cyber.incidents@usda.gov>; ASOD is staffed 24x7x365.
The incident is reported promptly to the ASOD CSIRT, OHS PDSD, and the OHS Insider Threat Program (if pertinent).
The OHS Special Security Officer (SSO) is often the person who reports the incident and notifies the ASOD CSIRT.
policy_statements.target: incident and notifies the ASOD CSIRT

policy_statements.source_text: If the ASOD CSIRT learns of the incident first, it notifies OHS PDSD.
conditions: If the ASOD CSIRT learns of the incident first

policy_statements.source_text: OHS PDSD is responsible for notifying and coordinating with the security staff of any external network owner if any external network may have been contaminated by a USDA CNSI spillage incident.
Operational security discipline must be used for all communication to minimize further exposure of the incident and damage to CNSI.
Specifically:
Provide only the minimum amount of information to convey that there has been an incident, then request a face-to-face meeting or a secure call;
Avoid indicating what the information is or its classification, unless using approved secure methods of communication;
conditions: unless using approved secure methods of communication

policy_statements.source_text: Only discuss the incident or potential incident with personnel who have an appropriate security clearance and a need to know; and
Refrain from contacting any individuals associated with the incident, as it may inhibit inquiry processes into potential security violations or insider threats.

OHS PDSD collaborates with the OHS National Security System Program (NSSP) as needed, the ASOD CSIRT, and network and system administrators who handle containment and cleanup activities, and consults with the OHS Insider Threat Program on any potential insider threat concerns.
OHS PDSD contacts the data owner of CNSI and agrees on details of steps needed for containment and cleanup.
OHS NSSP assists and advises in the containment and cleanup strategies and activities and coordination with classified network owners, as appropriate.
The contact information is 202-720-0594 or <OHSEC-NSSP-SupportTeam@dm.usda.gov>.

The ASOD CSIRT and OHS PDSD coordinate with US-CERT on all incident response activities and communications related to classified systems and CNSI spillage, sharing information about incidents, threats, and vulnerabilities to the extent consistent with standards and guidelines for NSS, issued in accordance with law and as directed by the President.

Identify and report the information system or system component contaminated by a potential or actual spillage, along with the specific information involved in the spillage, using operational security discipline.
Promptly isolate and secure the contaminated information system or system component.
The ASOD CSIRT, OHS PDSD, and OHS NSSP advise network owners and administrators on how to contain and isolate classified or potentially classified information.
policy_statements.actor_name: ASOD CSIRT, OHS PDSD, and OHS NSSP

policy_statements.source_text: Safeguard the information at all times.
The Senior Agency Official for CNSI/Director of OHS and the USDA CISO have the authority to direct any action, including shutdown, with respect to any system on which CNSI is spilled.
policy_statements.actor_name: Senior Agency Official for CNSI/Director of OHS and the USDA CISO
policy_statements.target: any system on which CNSI is spilled

policy_statements.source_text: The data owner may provide input on containment and cleanup strategies, over which OHS PDSD has approval authority.
policy_statements.target: input on containment and cleanup strategies, over which OHS PDSD has approval authority

policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD CSIRT investigates to determine if other information systems or system components may have been subsequently contaminated and communicates that information to OHS PDSD.

If an external network may have been contaminated by the spillage, the OHS NSSP and the ASOD CSIRT consult with the external network provider or providers to contain and isolate classified or potentially classified information.
policy_statements.actor_name: OHS NSSP and the ASOD CSIRT
conditions: If an external network may have been contaminated by the spillage

policy_statements.source_text: Eradicate the spilled information from all contaminated information systems and system components.
Other cleanup activities may be also be required.
Note that CNSI spillages involving cloud computing environments present unique challenges for eradication.

System, network, and database administrators document the steps taken to contain and clean up a CNSI spillage and provide that documentation to the ASOD CSIRT and OHS PDSD as proof that the actions were taken.
Certification is required to verify that the spilled information has been eradicated from the contaminated system(s) and device(s) and that the network is clean.
The following information pertains only to the cybersecurity aspects of a CNSI spillage.
Other investigative aspects may continue separately after the cybersecurity portion of the incident is closed.

The OHS SSO submits final security incident reports to the Senior Agency Official for CNSI, the USDA CISO, and the data owner, along with recommendations such as making changes to security controls or training.
policy_statements.target: to the Senior Agency Official for CNSI, the USDA CISO, and the data owner, along with recommendations such as making changes

policy_statements.source_text: The OHS SSO also submits recommendations for changes or improvements to the Senior Agency Official for CNSI and the USDA CISO.
OHS PDSD provides the final determination to close the CNSI spillage incident to the Senior Agency Official for CNSI and the USDA CISO.
For the ASOD CSIRT, the USDA CISO may deem the cybersecurity incident closed or identify additional steps to be taken before closure.
OHS’s Insider Threat Program must be involved:
As soon as an issue is identified; and
conditions: As soon as an issue is identified; and

policy_statements.source_text: In all incidents and inquiries potentially or actually relating to an insider’s use of access privileges to do harm, wittingly or unwittingly, to the security of the United States through espionage, terrorism, unauthorized disclosure of national security information, or the loss or degradation of Departmental resources or capabilities.
OHS Insider Threat Program’s contact information is 202-720-3487 or <insider@dm.usda.gov>.

The Insider Threat Program Coordinator conducts inquiries on all potential insider threat incidents and coordinates with appointed stakeholders, including within the Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO), to obtain information, including electronic records and files, necessary to identify, analyze, and resolve insider threat matters.

The Insider Threat Program serves as the USDA liaison to the intelligence community for insider threat and counterintelligence activities within the Department, to include referrals to the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI).
policy_statements.resulting_status: USDA liaison to the intelligence community for insider threat and counterintelligence activities within the Department

policy_statements.source_text: The Office of the Chief Financial Officer (OCFO) is consulted when an incident affects a financial system or financial records.
policy_statements.actor_name: Office of the Chief Financial Officer (OCFO)

policy_statements.source_text: After informing OC, OCFO is responsible for issuing notifications to financial services institutions such as banks, credit unions, payment card companies, and insurance companies about incidents affecting USDA’s financial systems or records.
OHRM, or agency and staff office personnel responsible for employee relations or adverse personnel actions must be notified when:
Incidents may require adverse personnel action due to actual or suspected misuse of information resources; or
policy_statements.actor_name: OHRM, or agency and staff office personnel responsible for employee relations or adverse personnel actions

policy_statements.source_text: It is necessary to take possession of GFE for investigations or confirmed incidents.
See Section 6h, Handling OIG-Related Incidents.
policy_statements.actor_name: OHRM, or agency and staff office personnel responsible for employee relations or adverse personnel actions

policy_statements.source_text: OGC provides legal advice for incidents involving other Government entities at the Federal, State, local, tribal, or territorial levels.
The ASOD CSIRT coordinates with the USDA CUI program office when CUI is exposed to an unauthorized person or persons.
The ASOD CSIRT must correlate and analyze current and historical incident information and responses to incidents to achieve a Departmentwide perspective on incident awareness and response.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: This Section describes incident management procedures from the perspective of agencies and staff offices.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Section 6 covers incident management procedures at the Departmental level.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Agencies and staff offices should leverage these procedures to produce their own tailored incident management procedures.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Incident preparation procedures are discussed in Section 10.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Incident management activities include incident detection; reporting incidents; investigating and analyzing incidents; gathering evidence and protecting sensitive incident information; mitigating incidents through activities such as containment, eradication, and recovery; documenting incidents; incident closure; and post-incident after-action reviews and improvement planning.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Many of these activities take place concurrently (e.g., investigating, mitigating, documenting) or occur multiple times (e.g., reporting with updates to original information).

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Prompt detection can improve incident response and recovery, thereby minimizing the resulting damage.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Incident management personnel receive indications, warnings, alerts, and notifications from a variety of sources about events that may be suspected and actual incidents.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: The sources include automated tools such as intrusion detection systems, anti-malware software, and log analyzers and reports from the ASOD CSIRT, other incident response groups, or users.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Incident management personnel and other personnel such as system, network, and database administrators must take actions directed by the ASOD CSIRT to detect potential or imminent threats and exploits.
policy_statements.actor_name: Incident management personnel and other personnel such as system, network, and database administrators

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Incident management personnel must expect to deal with false positives from any type of source.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: NIST SP 800-61 Revision 2, Section 3.2, Detection and Analysis, provides extensive details on the challenges, differences between precursors and indicators as signs of potential incidents, and tools or other sources that provide such signs.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Incident management personnel must log into the agency or staff office incident tracking mechanism all suspected and actual incidents, appropriate details, and conclusions of their investigations.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: This Section describes reporting topics that must be incorporated into agency and staff office procedures.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Procedures must indicate the types of suspected and actual incidents that must be reported immediately to the ASOD CSIRT.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Details about each incident must also be submitted using the forms described in this Section.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: All required information on the reporting forms must be finalized before an incident may be closed; supporting information may also be required.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Report all suspected or actual incidents affecting USDA information resources to the ASOD CSIRT through the ASOD 24-Hour Hotline (866-905-6890) or the Cyber mailbox (<cyber.incidents@ASOC.usda.gov>).

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Either communication method may be used to convey additional information about the reported incident.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Report all suspected or actual incidents to the ASOD CSIRT within 1 hour of discovery.
conditions: within 1 hour of discovery

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Examples of reportable incidents are:

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Suspected or actual spillage of CNSI or suspected or actual cybersecurity incidents affecting classified systems, with concurrent reporting to OHS PDSD, the agency or staff office Information Security Coordinator (ISC), and agency or staff office information security support staff.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: See Section 7b(3) for guidance to protect CNSI;

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Suspected or actual unauthorized release of CUI;

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Suspected or actual exposure or compromise of PII (a category of CUI) in all forms (e.g., cyber-based, verbal discussions of PII with unauthorized persons, loss of hardcopy documents that contain PII), whether the exposure is inadvertent or intentional;

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Caution: When reporting a PII breach, do not forward the subject PII to the ASOD CSIRT.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Do not delete emails or email attachments containing PII until receiving instructions on what to do.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Suspected or actual incidents related to criminal activity or misuse;

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Suspected or actual insider threats where an insider is using or may be using access privileges to do harm, wittingly or unwittingly, to the security of the United States, including damage to the United States through espionage, terrorism, unauthorized disclosure of national security information, or the loss or degradation of Departmental resources or capabilities; and

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Suspected or actual incidents of compromise to the confidentiality, integrity, or availability of USDA information, information systems, or information services.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: When reporting a classified or potentially classified incident, including spillage of CNSI, use operational security discipline for all communication to minimize further exposure of the incident and damage to CNSI.
conditions: When reporting a classified or potentially classified incident

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Specifically:

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Do not delete emails or email attachments with CNSI until receiving instructions on what to do;

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Do not forward the CNSI to the ASOD CSIRT, or anyone else;

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Provide only the minimum amount of information to convey that there has been an incident and request a face-to-face meeting or a secure call to follow up;

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Avoid indicating what the information is or its classification, unless using approved secure methods of communication; and
conditions: unless using approved secure methods of communication

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Only discuss the incident or potential incident with personnel who have an appropriate security clearance and a need to know.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Notify others with a need to know about the incident, based on the type of incident and the information resources affected.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Examples include the system owner, network, system, or database administrators, or the Mission Area Assistant CIO or Privacy Officer.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: As incident investigation and mitigation continue, incident management personnel are to provide the ASOD CSIRT with additional information such as the threat vector, functional and information impacts, mitigation details, or recoverability.
policy_statements.target: ASOD CSIRT with additional information such

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: An incident report is submitted to the ASOD CSIRT using these Departmental forms to close an incident:

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: AD-3038 for incident reports involving unauthorized access to PII or equipment with PII that is lost or stolen (including seizure by a foreign government; or

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: AD-3043 for all other incidents.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Fill in the information using the appropriate form.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: If the investigation determines that a reported incident is a false positive, only Section 1 of AD-3043 needs to be completed.
conditions: If the investigation determines that a reported incident is a false positive

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: All required information must be submitted before an incident may be closed.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: When PII is inadvertently released to a person or organization, at the discretion of management in collaboration with CPO and ASOD, outside USDA, the responsible agency or staff office in coordination with the CPO may send the recipient or recipients a tailored copy of form AD-3050, PII Incident Non Disclosure Agreement.
cross_references: AD-3050, PII Incident Non Disclosure Agreement
conditions: When PII is inadvertently released to a person or organization

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: The form must be tailored by modifying the paragraphs:

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: To describe the circumstances of the incident to indicate how the control of PII was lost (e.g., PII being sent in an email, as an attachment to an email, or on a lost hardcopy document);

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: To describe a set of actions the recipient should take to delete or destroy the email, file, or document containing PII and not to discuss or disclose the PII; and

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: To provide instructions where to return the completed form.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Log this activity and any responses in the tracking mechanism of the responsible agency or staff office.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: All suspected and actual incidents must be investigated.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Agency and staff offices must coordinate and collaborate with the ASOD CSIRT.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: They must not directly contact external entities such as US-CERT unless specifically requested to do so by the ASOD Director or ASOD CSIRT personnel to whom that authority has been delegated.
conditions: unless specifically requested to do so by the ASOD Director or ASOD CSIRT personnel to whom that authority has been delegated

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Agency and staff office incident management personnel may request assistance, as needed, from the ASOD CSIRT; US-CERT or other support resources for incident handling must be requested through the ASOD CSIRT.
policy_statements.actor_name: Agency and staff office incident management personnel

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: The ASOD Director or authorized ASOD CSIRT personnel may request agency and staff office incident management personnel to provide technical or investigation assistance to other agencies or staff offices.
policy_statements.actor_name: ASOD Director or authorized ASOD CSIRT personnel

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Investigations of some incidents need the involvement or leadership of other entities with specialized authorities and capabilities.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: Agency and staff office personnel are expected to cooperate in these investigations.

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: The other entities include:

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: OIG or law enforcement from any level of government (Federal, State, local, tribal, or territorial) for criminal activity;
policy_statements.actor_name: OIG or law enforcement from any level of government (Federal, State, local, tribal, or territorial)

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: OIG for instances of fraud, waste, and abuse;
policy_statements.target: instances of fraud, waste, and abuse

policy_statements.section_title: Agency and Staff Office Incident Management Procedures
policy_statements.source_text: OHS PDSD for actual or potential compromises of CNSI;
